Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons recognized by law as Women. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

(2) Prevention of violence against women and children includes:

a. prevention of violence in the family and community environment including villages;
b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and
d. prevention of violence in public transportation
(3) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) may be conducted in the form of:
a. socialization especially to vulnerable groups;
b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:
d. forming and facilitating groups or forums for children, adolescents, women and the community;
e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.
(4) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling family affairs, community and village empowerment, information affairs and those handling women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.
(8) Implementation of violence prevention against women and children is carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, the business community, communities, children and youth groups, mass media and other related parties.

CHAPTER VI

SERVICES

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

Article 30

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Higher Education Institutions implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

(1) Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.

(2) Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

CHAPTER X GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

(1) Guidance and supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted by the regency government and village government.

(2) Guidance and supervision by the regency government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

(3) Guidance and supervision by the village government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the village level.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include: a.guidelines and service operational standards;

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(5) Guidance and supervision shall be conducted at least once a year and its implementation shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and Child Protection affairs and the Regional Inspectorate.

(6) The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be reported to the Regent and submitted to relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations, Village Government, community and business sector.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

B A B V

PREVENTION OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 24

(1) The community and business community have the right to participate in the prevention of violence cases against women and children, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) can be carried out individually or collectively, whether individually or institutionally.

Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is organized based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discriminatory; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

CHAPTER XII FINANCING

Article 29

The costs of administering protection for women and children victims of violence shall be sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. other sources that are lawful and non-binding in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

(2) Prevention of violence against women and children includes:

a. prevention of violence in the family and community environment including villages;
b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and
d. prevention of violence in public transportation
(3) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) may be conducted in the form of:
a. socialization especially to vulnerable groups;
b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:
d. forming and facilitating groups or forums for children, adolescents, women and the community;
e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.
(4) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling family affairs, community and village empowerment, information affairs and those handling women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.
(8) Implementation of violence prevention against women and children is carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, the business community, communities, children and youth groups, mass media and other related parties.

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER X GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

(1) Guidance and supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted by the regency government and village government.

(2) Guidance and supervision by the regency government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

(3) Guidance and supervision by the village government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the village level.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include: a.guidelines and service operational standards;

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(5) Guidance and supervision shall be conducted at least once a year and its implementation shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and Child Protection affairs and the Regional Inspectorate.

(6) The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be reported to the Regent and submitted to relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations, Village Government, community and business sector.

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

(2) Prevention of violence against women and children includes:

a. prevention of violence in the family and community environment including villages;
b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and
d. prevention of violence in public transportation
(3) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) may be conducted in the form of:
a. socialization especially to vulnerable groups;
b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:
d. forming and facilitating groups or forums for children, adolescents, women and the community;
e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.
(4) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling family affairs, community and village empowerment, information affairs and those handling women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.
(8) Implementation of violence prevention against women and children is carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, the business community, communities, children and youth groups, mass media and other related parties.

CHAPTER VI

SERVICES

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER X GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

(1) Guidance and supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted by the regency government and village government.

(2) Guidance and supervision by the regency government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

(3) Guidance and supervision by the village government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the village level.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include: a.guidelines and service operational standards;

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(5) Guidance and supervision shall be conducted at least once a year and its implementation shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and Child Protection affairs and the Regional Inspectorate.

(6) The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be reported to the Regent and submitted to relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations, Village Government, community and business sector.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is organized based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discriminatory; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

Article 30

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Higher Education Institutions implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 24

(1) The community and business community have the right to participate in the prevention of violence cases against women and children, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) can be carried out individually or collectively, whether individually or institutionally.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

(1) Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.

(2) Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

Article 26

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary as needed.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is organized based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discriminatory; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

(2) Prevention of violence against women and children includes:

a. prevention of violence in the family and community environment including villages;
b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and
d. prevention of violence in public transportation
(3) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) may be conducted in the form of:
a. socialization especially to vulnerable groups;
b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:
d. forming and facilitating groups or forums for children, adolescents, women and the community;
e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.
(4) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling family affairs, community and village empowerment, information affairs and those handling women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.
(8) Implementation of violence prevention against women and children is carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, the business community, communities, children and youth groups, mass media and other related parties.

CHAPTER VI

SERVICES

CHAPTER X GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

(1) Guidance and supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted by the regency government and village government.

(2) Guidance and supervision by the regency government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

(3) Guidance and supervision by the village government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the village level.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include: a.guidelines and service operational standards;

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(5) Guidance and supervision shall be conducted at least once a year and its implementation shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and Child Protection affairs and the Regional Inspectorate.

(6) The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be reported to the Regent and submitted to relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations, Village Government, community and business sector.

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER VIII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 24

(1) The community and business community have the right to participate in the prevention of violence cases against women and children, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) can be carried out individually or collectively, whether individually or institutionally.

Article 30

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Higher Education Institutions implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

(1) Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.

(2) Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;

Article 20

(5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisor; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons recognized by law as Women. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Article 27

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 23

(1) Integrated service for the protection of women and children (PTPPA) at the village or urban village level is carried out by the Village or Urban Village Post. (2) The establishment and facilitation of the implementation of the Village or Urban Village Post is the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization which handles the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection and the Village Government. (3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks of: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing accompaniment services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-District and Regency Integrated Service Centers as well as to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services; f. conducting case handling coordination; g. conducting data collection on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (4) The Integrated Service Center for the protection of women and children (PPTPPA) as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. village or urban village government; b. health clinic and/or village or urban village midwife; c. family empowerment and welfare; d. community organizations; e. religious organizations; f. community-based service institutions; g. women's organizations; and h. religious leaders, community leaders and traditional leaders. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisor; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and

b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:

e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.

(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons recognized by law as Women. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

(2) Prevention of violence against women and children includes:

a. prevention of violence in the family and community environment including villages;
b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and
d. prevention of violence in public transportation
(3) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) may be conducted in the form of:
a. socialization especially to vulnerable groups;
b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:
d. forming and facilitating groups or forums for children, adolescents, women and the community;
e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.
(4) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling family affairs, community and village empowerment, information affairs and those handling women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.
(8) Implementation of violence prevention against women and children is carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, the business community, communities, children and youth groups, mass media and other related parties.

SERVICES

CHAPTER X GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

(1) Guidance and supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted by the regency government and village government.

(2) Guidance and supervision by the regency government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

(3) Guidance and supervision by the village government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the village level.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include: a.guidelines and service operational standards;

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(5) Guidance and supervision shall be conducted at least once a year and its implementation shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and Child Protection affairs and the Regional Inspectorate.

(6) The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be reported to the Regent and submitted to relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations, Village Government, community and business sector.

Article 30

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Higher Education Institutions implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is organized based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discriminatory; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER XII FINANCING

Article 29

The costs of administering protection for women and children victims of violence shall be sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. other sources that are lawful and non-binding in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 23

(1) Integrated service for the protection of women and children (PTPPA) at the village or urban village level is carried out by the Village or Urban Village Post. (2) The establishment and facilitation of the implementation of the Village or Urban Village Post is the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization which handles the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection and the Village Government. (3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks of: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing accompaniment services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-District and Regency Integrated Service Centers as well as to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services; f. conducting case handling coordination; g. conducting data collection on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (4) The Integrated Service Center for the protection of women and children (PPTPPA) as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. village or urban village government; b. health clinic and/or village or urban village midwife; c. family empowerment and welfare; d. community organizations; e. religious organizations; f. community-based service institutions; g. women's organizations; and h. religious leaders, community leaders and traditional leaders. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisor; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

(1) Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.

(2) Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons recognized by law as Women. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. CHAPTER IX MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 25

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to identify developments and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations implementing policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.

(4) Monitoring shall be conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Article 30

(1) The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or Non-Governmental Organizations and Higher Education Institutions implementing protection for women and children victims of violence.

(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

(2) Prevention of violence against women and children includes:

a. prevention of violence in the family and community environment including villages;
b. prevention of violence in the education environment;
c. prevention of violence in the workplace environment; and
d. prevention of violence in public transportation
(3) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) may be conducted in the form of:
a. socialization especially to vulnerable groups;
b. publications, cultural performances, youth jamborees and campaigns;
c. training:
d. forming and facilitating groups or forums for children, adolescents, women and the community;
e. encouraging/establishing educational institutions as violence-free zones against women and children;
f. establishing child-friendly regencies.
(4) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling family affairs, community and village empowerment, information affairs and those handling women's empowerment and child protection affairs.
(5) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling education affairs, including religious education.
(6) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling manpower affairs, trade and industry affairs, and small and medium enterprises and cooperatives affairs.
(7) Prevention of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is the responsibility of Regional Apparatus Organizations handling market affairs, public works affairs, information affairs and transportation affairs.
(8) Implementation of violence prevention against women and children is carried out by involving community organizations, non-governmental organizations, legal aid institutions, the business community, communities, children and youth groups, mass media and other related parties.

CHAPTER VI

SERVICES

CHAPTER X GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 27

(1) Guidance and supervision of the administration of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted by the regency government and village government.

(2) Guidance and supervision by the regency government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.

(3) Guidance and supervision by the village government as referred to in paragraph (1) shall cover the administration of protection for women and children at the village level.

(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include: a.guidelines and service operational standards;

b.routine coordination; c. technical guidance and training, provision of facilities and infrastructure and human resources;

d.monitoring and evaluation;

e. reporting.

(5) Guidance and supervision shall be conducted at least once a year and its implementation shall be the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization in charge of women's empowerment and Child Protection affairs and the Regional Inspectorate.

(6) The results of the implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (5) shall be reported to the Regent and submitted to relevant Regional Apparatus Organizations, Village Government, community and business sector.

Article 23

(1) Integrated service for the protection of women and children (PTPPA) at the village or urban village level is carried out by the Village or Urban Village Post. (2) The establishment and facilitation of the implementation of the Village or Urban Village Post is the responsibility of the Regional Apparatus Organization which handles the affairs of women's empowerment and child protection and the Village Government. (3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks of: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing accompaniment services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-District and Regency Integrated Service Centers as well as to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services; f. conducting case handling coordination; g. conducting data collection on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (4) The Integrated Service Center for the protection of women and children (PPTPPA) as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. village or urban village government; b. health clinic and/or village or urban village midwife; c. family empowerment and welfare; d. community organizations; e. religious organizations; f. community-based service institutions; g. women's organizations; and h. religious leaders, community leaders and traditional leaders. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisor; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions. (6) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established through a decree of the village head or urban village head.

Article 2

Protection of women and children victims of violence is organized based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. gender equality and justice; c. non-discriminatory; d. protection of victims' rights; e. legal certainty.

Article 26

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary as needed.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 8

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 5 letters c and d who are legally fully responsible for preventing all forms of violence and protecting women and children as family members.

Article 9

(1) Prevention is intended to reduce the potential risk and vulnerability of women and children from all forms of violence occurring both in the domestic and public spheres, including preventing the recurrence of violence experienced by victims.

Article 23

(3) The Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) is established with the tasks of: a. providing complaint services; b. providing counseling services; c. providing accompaniment services; d. providing referral services to the Sub-District and Regency Integrated Service Centers as well as to other related parties; e. providing social reintegration services; f. conducting case handling coordination; g. conducting data collection on case handling at the village or urban village level; h. conducting prevention at the village or urban village level. (5) The structure of the Village or Urban Village Post as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of: a. advisor; b. chairperson; c. secretary; and d. divisions.
