CHAPTER XI REPORTING

Article 28

(1) The Regent shall be responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of Minimum Service Standards in the field of integrated services for women and children victims of violence to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

(2) Reporting on implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Muna Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Muna Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muna. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Muna Regency. 5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia, can experience menstruation, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and includes persons recognized by law as Women. 7. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including a child in the womb. 8. Violence is any act against a person that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life. 10. Violence against children is any act against children that results in suffering or distress physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, serious wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, indecency, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ utilization, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to gain material or immaterial benefits. 15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences physical suffering, psychological suffering, sexual suffering, either directly or indirectly resulting from acts of violence. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line up or down to the third degree. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of violence to resolve the problems faced. 21. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs. 22. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles properly both in the family and in society. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance. 25. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, Safe Houses, Children's Social Protection Houses, Trauma Center Protection Houses, Women's Social Protection Houses, Shelters, etc. 26. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter abbreviated as SPM is a benchmark for service performance of integrated service units in providing report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 27. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related services, vertical agencies, and communities, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe House is a temporary residence provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 29. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group or class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs resulting from the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life. 30.

CHAPTER VII INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 20

(1) Services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) are carried out through an integrated service mechanism.

(2) Integrated services as referred to in paragraph (1) are established at the regency, sub-district and village or urban village levels.
